description.value: The study identified brain regions where abnormally low glucose uptake measured by FDG-PET correlates with executive and behavioral dysfunction in patients with frontotemporal lobar degeneration and control subjects.

spans.text: Accordingly, the objective of our current study was to identify brain regions where abnormally low glucose uptake as measured by [ 18 F]fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) correlates with executive and behavioral dysfunction in a cohort of patients with FTLD.

value: We hypothesized that executive dysfunctions would be associated with frontomedial and frontolateral hypometabolism, particularly in the anterior cingulate cortex and the inferior frontal junction area.
For behavioral deficits, we expected a correlation with hypometabolism, particularly in frontomedial/orbitofrontal cortices and the insula.

description.value: A pilot observational study of patients with frontotemporal lobar degeneration and cognitively healthy control subjects.

spans.text: Our pilot study reveals partially overlapping neural correlates of executive and behavioral dysfunction in frontotemporal lobar degeneration.

value: Executive dysfunction was significantly correlated with glucose hypometabolism in several frontomedian areas, left frontolateral regions, the left insula, the left globus pallidus, caudatum and thalamus. These findings support the results of previous studies indicating that executive control depends on frontal structures in particular.
